name: Scheduled Updates
description: Schedule field-value changes on any entity type (nodes, users, terms, files) to run at a future time via cron.
project_description:
The Scheduled Updates module allows scheduling updates at a specific date and time to entities such as Content (nodes), Users, Terms, Files and many more. Update dates can contain 1 or multiple fields. Since many things are fields in Drupal this means you can also update properties like published, promoted, sticky, title and pretty much anything else you can think of.

AI was used on the 3.0.x branch to bring it up to Drupal 10.4/11 standards; the maintainers ask that it be tested heavily.

The module supports two different types of updates:

Embedded Updates: created on the add/edit form of the entity they will update (via an entity-reference field and Inline Entity Form). Example uses: scheduling publish and/or unpublish dates directly on node forms; setting a user to inactive at a certain date on the user edit form.

Independent Updates: added directly through their own forms. The user selects the nodes, users or other entities they would like to update; a single independent update can target multiple entities. Example uses: select a group of nodes to be promoted and/or published on a certain date; select a group of users to be given a Manager role at the beginning of the next month.

Configuration: before making updates you must first create at least one Scheduled Update Type. A Scheduled Update Type can only target one entity type to update, and is either embedded or independent. To easily create embedded updates click 'Add Update Field' on the Manage Fields page of the entity type you want to update. To create a scheduled update type go to Configuration -> Workflow -> Scheduled Updates -> Scheduled Update Types. After creating a type you choose the fields from your target entity type to include on the update type (a field map from update fields to target fields). Alternatives include scheduler, scheduled_publish, scheduled_transitions and advanced_scheduler.
